newsitem.title: UK: THE PROTEUS COLUMN - China after Deng.
newsitem.headline: THE PROTEUS COLUMN - China after Deng.

text.p: THE PROTEUS COLUMN

The grand architect of Chinese reform is dead but the economic house built by Deng Xiaoping in the last 18 years of his life has sound foundations and is in no danger of tumbling, and foreign insurers investing in China have nothing to fear.

That is the message being delivered by analysts and diplomats in the wake of the death last night of Deng Xiaoping, paramount leader of China. Deng is being credited with turning a backward Stalinist nation into an emerging economic superpower and appears to have left his heirs with little room for manoeuvre.

Phrases such as "the alternatives are almost non-existent," and "the economic policies that Deng helped to establish are irreversible," are being used, and the idea being flagged is that the Chinese Communist Party depends on economic reform to sustain its own mandate.

Western insurers, attracted by the huge potential market, have been clamouring to get into China as economic reforms have taken effect. And they have managed to secure a relatively strong position with the Chinese authorities.
A good example of this came last week when China put off plans for a national reinsurance pool following strong opposition from both mainland and foreign insurance companies.

National pool reinsurers are a common enough way of keeping insurance premiums in the country. However, foreign reinsurance practitioners claimed China's insurance market was not mature enough to implement the plan, and said it would deprive mainland insurers of the chance to learn from foreign insurance companies and brokers because they would need to negotiate only with the People's Insurance Co of China for reinsurance business, if the national pool were set up.
Wintherthur, the first Europan insurer to be granted a licence in China, said this morning it was confident there would be no change in the situation for foreign insurers following Deng's death.
If the new leadership of China can keep things going in the same direction, international insurers will continue to expend time and energy building friendships in this potentially huge market.
